stem:
Esha folds two paper wedges for a craft display. The diagram shows angle $J$ and angle $K$.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims correctly decide which angle is larger by overlaying?

options.text: Match the vertices and align one arm; the free arm of angle $K$ opens farther, so angle $K$ is larger.
Judge which opening is larger while the vertices stay apart on the desk.
After the vertices coincide and one arm is aligned, the free arm that sticks out farther belongs to the larger angle.
The printed letter names $J$ and $K$ alone decide which angle is larger.

teacher.key_rationale: Overlay requires coinciding vertices and one aligned arm; the free arm that opens farther marks the larger angle. Here that is angle K. Judging with vertices apart omits the overlay condition. Letter names alone are not a size test.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as two separate paper-wedge angles J (narrow) and K (wider).
